definition: Vicissitude means an unpredictable change in circumstances, usually an unwelcome one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word vicissitude. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know vicissitude should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Ten seasons in the league taught her every vicissitude of the sport: two trades, a lockout, a torn tendon, and a coach who never learned her name.
A hiccup is far milder than a vicissitude — a small snag smoothed over by lunchtime, not a real turn of fortune.
A catastrophe is stronger than a vicissitude — vicissitudes are the turns a life absorbs and continues past, while a catastrophe can end the story outright.

An upheaval is a violent, large-scale disruption — a revolution, a market collapse — that overturns the whole order of things at once. A vicissitude is smaller and more patient: one of fortune's ordinary unwelcome turns, the kind a long life absorbs several of and continues past.

A reversal is one specific shape of bad luck: fortune that was running your way flips against you — the verdict overturned, the lead lost. A vicissitude needs no prior success to spoil; it is any unpredictable turn of circumstances, arriving from any direction, usually unwelcome.

A twist of fate is the storyteller's phrase for a single dramatic turn, and the twist can be a jackpot as happily as a downfall. Vicissitude drops the wonder and keeps the weariness: fortune's unwelcome turns taken together, the standard weather of any long life.
